titre: How the scoring grid is measured.
lede: This page shows what the scoring numbers are made of: which dossiers, which factors, which declared tables, and where each figure is not quoted. No real person exists in the sealed public record, and no official risk list was copied into it: that refusal is enforced by a test and not by discipline.
description: Which dossiers, which factors, which declared tables, and where a figure is not quoted. No real person is in the record, and a test enforces that.

html: The measured half rests on dossiers we wrote and we declare: six escalated typologies and, deliberately, their six retained files: a family company with each ownership layer named against the shell that hides them, a neighbourhood shop whose turnover sits on its declaration against the counter that outruns it, a salaried account at ratio one against the firm at ratio five, a foreign student at stipend scale against the remote newcomer at several times his declaration. What separates each file is in the fields, history and ratios, never only in the label, and a test pins all six pairs structurally.

No official country list was copied, and a test makes the refusal structural: escalated and retained files share their countries of residence, so no code can quietly become a list. The geography factor scores zero on this book, on both sides, and the page above states this as a finding and does not hide it.

verif.p: The suite revalidates each written dossier, the six file pairs, and the country-sharing rule.

cmd.n: 84 dossiers revalidated, file invariants and the no-list rule pinned

sections.h2: Each table is declared, and declared as an assumption
html: A scoring factor needs tables: which activities weigh what, which products, which channels. Each table in this tool is written in one file with provenance, unit and bounds, and each one carries the same one-word status: assumed. That is the thesis of Scoring: the tables your vendor calls calibration are declarations, and the only way to know what they are worth is to measure them against your own dispositioned reviews.

verif.p: The tables file carries value, provenance and bounds for each assumption.

cmd.n: the assumptions cases pin provenance and bounds

sections.h2: Generated variants, apart whichever side they favour
html: The synthetic half is generated from the written dossiers under an explicit seed, natures preserved by construction: linked factors keep the observed-over-declared ratios, cash shares stay on their side of the line, ownership layers keep their floor, the remote newcomer stays new. On this tool the generated half is harsher than the written one on the best factor, and it stays apart exactly as it would if it flattered: separation is a rule and not a convenience, and the page shows both numbers side by side.

verif.p: Open the record: the two blocks carry their provenance in the data itself.

cmd.n: prints the two provenance declarations: written by hand, seeded variants

sections.h2: Wilson everywhere, scores bounded, refusals where n is small
html: Each rate travels with its Wilson interval at 95 percent and its n; below twenty observations a rate is noted and not quoted, and recall on your own book is refused outright under five confirmed escalations. A factor's score lives in [0, 1] and a value outside it is an error named with the factor and the dossier, never a silent rounding. The threshold grid is shared and inclusive, so the strictest cell still means something for a factor that answers exactly one.

verif.p: The bounds and refusals live in code, and the suite exercises them.

cmd.n: interval, score-bound and refusal cases run with the rest
